corridor_note: P8005 is a short (6.1 km, sheet) spur carrying regasified/imported gas from the SUMED Ain Sokhna terminal into GASCO's national grid. The Egyptian Ministry of Petroleum's own magazine (petro-mag.org, Nov 2025 issue, GASCO feature) reads 'خط استيراد الغاز من ميناء سوميد بالعين السخنة' -- literally 'gas import line from the SUMED port AT AIN SOKHNA' -- which settles this pass's routing question: the terminal is Ain Sokhna on the Red Sea/Gulf of Suez, NOT Sidi Kerir on the Mediterranean. The grid-side tie-in has never been named in any source across at least four prior GEM research passes on this row (2026-07-28 through 2026-08-11, per docs/country_notes/egypt.md) nor in this one. Ain Sokhna hosts several GASCO compressor/metering facilities within roughly 5-8 km of the SUMED terminal -- geographically consistent with a 6.1 km connector -- but naming a specific one without a source would be a guess, not a finding.
length_check: 6.1 km (sheet) is geographically plausible for a short terminal-to-grid connector at Ain Sokhna, where GASCO facilities cluster within a few km of the SUMED terminal. Cannot be checked as an endpoint-to-endpoint chord because the grid-side endpoint is unresolved.
notes: Settles the Ain Sokhna vs Sidi Kerir question the task raised: Ain Sokhna, confirmed. The live sheet's ResearcherNotes (Nagwa) states this line feeds the New Capital Power Station and flags that GEM's pipeline name duplicates SUMED's own crude-OIL pipeline name -- a naming collision in GEM's own data, not evidence of a different physical route; not independently verified in this pass, just carried forward as context. The World Bank ESIA PDF cited in the sheet's Status[ref] (SFG1795-EA-P116194-PUBLIC-Disclosed-2-9-2016.pdf) verified live (200) but concerns the Giza North Power Station, an unrelated project -- flagging so it is not mistaken for route corroboration of this pipeline.

duplicate_assessment: P8055 ('Trans-Sinai Gas Pipeline II', 28 km, sourced to GASCO's own -- now dead, unarchived -- grid-expansion PDF, staged in the 2026-08-07 batch) and P8009 ('Abr Sinai Gas Pipeline II' / 'Pipeline 2', 27 km per the Nov 2025 petro-mag.org issue or 28 km per the Dec 2024 issue, staged in the 2026-07-27/28 batch) are very likely the SAME physical pipeline entered twice, under two different names, from two different documents, by the same researcher (GEM's own initials column reads NA/Nagwa across this row family per prior notes). Evidence assembled in this pass: (1) 'Trans-Sinai' and 'Abr Sinai' are two English renderings of the same Arabic phrase, 'عبر سيناء' -- GASCO's own English-language materials use both interchangeably (the EIB's 2007 EIA is literally titled 'GASCO Abr Sinai Onshore Gas Pipeline' while GASCO's grid-expansion PDF, per the escalation-note paraphrase, calls the equivalent project 'Trans-Sinai'). (2) The lengths match exactly at 28 km between P8055 (GASCO PDF) and P8009's Dec 2024 petro-mag.org reading (28 km) -- the Nov 2025 petro-mag.org issue's 27 km for the same row is presumably an updated/rounded figure for the same still-under-construction line, not a different pipe. (3) Both sources independently describe their subject as a DUPLICATION (ازدواج) of the pre-existing Abr Sinai/Trans-Sinai pipeline (i.e. of GEM's own already-mapped P8044), not as a new corridor -- the same relationship, described the same way, in two unrelated documents. (4) Construction timing overlaps: petro-mag.org's Dec 2024 and Nov 2025 issues both carry this as 'under construction'; GASCO's PDF is dated December 2024 (per its own URL path); and an Akhbar El-Yom article from April 2026 (cited on P8009's record above) confirms land-compensation negotiations for a 'phase 2' of a Sinai gas-pipeline duplication project were still active as of that date -- a multi-year timeline consistent with one ongoing project being tracked by three independent documents at three different points in its life, rather than two separate, coincidentally-identical 28 km duplication projects. (5) A prior GEM pass had already established that P8055's claimed lineage to a 'Trans Gulf ... II' family (P8013, a 12-inch oilfield crude line) is FALSE and that GASCO's own material instead calls it a duplication of the Trans-Sinai/Abr Sinai line -- i.e. the SAME project family that P8008/P8009 belong to, once the false P8013 lineage is set aside. By contrast, P8008 (15.5 km, 'Pipeline 1', completed June 2024) does not match P8055 on length and is very likely a distinct, earlier-completed stretch of the same 'Abr Sinai II' duplication program, not the P8055 duplicate. Caveat: GASCO's PDF could not be independently re-read in this pass (confirmed dead, HTTP 404, no Wayback capture at any timestamp -- see P8055's urls_verified) -- this assessment rests on the prior escalation note's direct paraphrase of that document plus the circumstantial evidence assembled above, not on a firsthand re-read. Recommendation for Update: flag P8009 and P8055 as candidate duplicates for human adjudication (do not auto-merge); if confirmed, retain whichever row carries better/live sourcing (currently P8009, via petro-mag.org, since P8055's sole primary source is now unreachable) and archive/cross-reference the other.
